recipes.name: Chef John's Sausage & Shrimp Jambalaya
ingredients_raw: 8 ounces andouille sausage, cut into 1/4-inch slices
1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place butter and sausage in a large stockpot over medium heat; cook and stir until sausage begins to brown, 5 to 6 minutes.
Stir in paprika, cumin, and cayenne; cook for 1 minute.
Stir tomatoes, celery, green pepper, green onions, salt, and bay leaf into the sausage mixture.
Add brown rice and stir to combine. Stir in chicken stock, bring it to a simmer, then turn heat to low. Cover and cook until rice is just tender, about 45 minutes.
Stir in shrimp, replace lid and cook until shrimp are cooked through, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Sausage & Shrimp Jambalaya
raw_recipe.description: Shrimp jambalaya with sausage is a comforting dish, stewed full of flavor, with rice cooked right in with the other ingredients for a hearty meal.

video.description: Get ready to spice up your taste buds with our flavorful Sausage and Shrimp Jambalaya! This Cajun-inspired dish is a symphony of bold and robust flavors that will transport you straight to the heart of New Orleans. Savor the smoky goodness of andouille sausage, perfectly cooked shrimp, and a medley of aromatic vegetables, all simmered together in a rich and zesty tomato-based sauce. Every bite is a burst of mouthwatering goodness, with the heat of spices and the comforting combination of textures. Whether you're hosting a festive gathering or simply craving a taste of Louisiana, our Sausage and Shrimp Jambalaya is a must-try culinary experience that will leave you wanting more.

review.reviewBody: I love me some Chef John. This was a really great recipe; I just modified it a bit based on taste preference and ingredient availability. Instead of butter I just used olive oil, and since I couldn't find Andouille, I just bought a different smoked sausage. I added some hot sauce for a bit of extra heat, I used a large can of diced tomates, I used two green peppers instead of one, I used wild rice instead of brown, and I used chicken instead of shrimp. Tasted quite delicious!

This was a solid recipe, with a really good rice to meat/aromatic vegetable ratio. I did make some changes. I used fresh prawns, so it instead of chicken broth I used (and made) a broth out of the shells, heads plus aromatic vegetables. The end result was very flavorful, but I might do a mix of chicken and shrimp broth next time. I also used parboiled rice instead of brown, because it holds the texture with higher amounts of liquid without becoming mushy, and it absorbs flavor really well. The cook time of the prawns was perfect: not too raw, not rubbery either. I fried and set aside the sausage like some people suggested, and added it about five minutes before adding the shrimp. Since I was in Spain, I used what was available to me (chorizo). I don't know if it still counts as jambalaya, but the flavor blew my mind.

Loved this recipe! Basically followed it for preference but didn't change much. Used yellow onion for the green in the Trinity, red bell because hubs, and added jalapeno for more heat. Only had white rice so simmered twenty minutes and then added the rice and additional cooked, shredded chicken for the last twenty before adding the shrimps. Nice, spicy and delicious! Will make again!

I am very disappointed. First of all Jambalaya is not a soup. It is not gumbo. It should not be liquidy when finished. I followed the instructions and my rice was way over cooked like mush, and I had to scoop out 2 cups of liquid. That's not what jambalaya is supposed to be.

This was AWESOME!!! While I mostly try to adhere to the recipe as written - I have a hard time not adding some garlic when it sounds right and, for this recipe - I added a minced jalapeño from my over abundant garden. I also have to agree - after adding the 1/2c tomatoes this called for - I ended up quickly chopping and adding another 1/2c before adding the brown rice - which was perfect.

The heat and flavors were spot on, but - a tad spicy for my husband. He finished his bowl but said he was starting to sweat! Not me - but maybe, MAYBE next time I will reduce the paprika to 1 TBLS. Also - thanks to another reviewer, while I stirred in the brown rice, when I added the stock/broth - I brought to a boil before covering and reducing heat. This made cook time right on. As always Chef John thank you for another delicious meal!!

Great recipe! As others mentioned, a few tweaks were made. We like it HOT 🔥 in our house so I added another pinch (or two) of cayenne, I used hot Italian sausage without the casing and then did a quick crumble saute of 2 links I had left over and added that to the "sauce", I used Rotelle HOT diced tomatoes and then also added a little more cooked brown rice with the shrimp to thicken the mixture. Probably no longer a jambalaya after all my mods but it was a big hit for my family and the flavor was AMAZING! Can't wait to make it again and try some other ideas!
I only used unsalted everything , 1/2 c rice and 1 1/2 c broth and 1/2 tsp low sodium salt it was very flavorful everything else I used the recipe quantity. It was awesome

Wow! I just added a little diced chicken, used hot Italian sausages and cut back a little on the cayenne pepper (the sausages were hot). Then I let it soak up the flavours in the fridge over night, fantastic! I'll make this again, thanks for the recipe. And of course some fresh baked cornbread too.

We love this and I have made it many many times over last few years. I cut the cayenne in half at first and add as I taste. Some in family do not like as spicy. I also usually cook brown rice separate in chicken stock to cut down on time.

I have made this several time. My family loves it. I do though add chicken thighs. I season with Tabasco, and Worcestershire. I save my shrimp tails, and shells, to make a stock. Instead of the chicken stock. On special days I add crab, legs. Mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm
We loved Chef Johns Jambalaya. It had just the right amount of heat for us. The only thing I did different was cook the rice separately, and because of that I did not add as much chicken stock.
This is a favorite go to....it is easy and most of the ingredients are easy to find!

This is really good. My husband loved it. One of my two kids did as well (the other just doesn’t like shrimp. But we made her eat it anyways.). I like reading all the reviews and seeing the tweaks. So we don’t eat rice, so I use frozen cauliflower rice and make that separately and keep it separate or else would become mush. I browned the sausage first then removed it. Wasn’t sure how the kids would do with it, but ended adding it back into the whole pot at the end. I doubled the recipe. sautéed two yellow onions, five celery, sticks, and two green peppers in the butter and some oil, then added the spices and a can of unsalted petite diced tomatoes (that’s all I had) and sautéed a few more mins . I used half the paprika and 3/4 of the cumin as someone else had suggested and I liked this. We don’t do spicy so I didn’t use cayenne. The andouille sausage added spice enough for our kids. I used homemade chicken broth, unsalted, half what the recipe called for since I wasn’t making rice, let the veggies simmer till tender, then added the shrimp in for five minutes, which was a perfect cooking time. I used frozen shrimp, defrosted it under cold, running water and stuck it back in the fridge to use later in the day. This worked great. And then just added a scoop or two of the finished product to a bowl of lightly salted cauliflower rice and it was delicious! Did need a little additional salt since I used unsalted broth and tomatoes.
I used mild Italian and smoked paprika as that's all I had. Excellent but I would use regular paprika next time.

I cook this quite a bit. The flavors are great and it makes plenty so I can have it as another meal later. It takes about an hour to make, with the prep, but mostly because of the cook time for the rice. It's definitely worth the time and effort!

Once again, Chef John created a masterpiece. I was a bit hesitant on using brown rice but I will never make it without it. Lovely add. It may be the brand of andouille that I buy but I find that if I leave the sausage in the whole time (the rice cooking process), it seems to leach out the flavor. So I brown the sausage, remove it from the recipe then proceed, tossing the sausage back in when I add the shrimp.

I purchased short-grain brown rice just for this recipe because I didn't trust myself to make the adjustments for the Basmati we usually eat. Unfortunately, the rice wasn't done after 45 minutes. It actually took an additional 30 minutes and additional liquid before the rice was done. Thankfully, the finished dish was worth it! This was the first time I have attempted Cajun dish and my husband immediately said, "This is good, babe" (we're lifelong Midwesterners). This will definitely be part of the winter rotation, now that we have easy access to Andouille sausage.

Made it exactly like the recipe. Very good with just the right amount of heat. Will definitely make again with one change. I will cook the rice separately and serve on the side. I always seem to end up with mushy rice when I cook it along with the rest of the ingredients!

pretty much followed the recipe but did add chicken. Also cut spices in half but could have maybe used 3/4 instead. Used large can of diced tomatoes. Used Italian sausage (3) from Costco. Baked in oven until almost cooked and then added to pot. I did cook the long grain (not Minute Rice) rice separately and added it to the pot. Used 1 cup rice . Used directions on rice package.
